text:
Darcy Kuemper played his 500th NHL game on Nov. 12, and the Kings marked it with special T-shirts and a ceremony. The night went badly, four goals against the Islanders, and it fit the season so far. He is 5-5-1 with an .873 save rate and has allowed 7.6 goals more than the shots he faced would usually produce, ninth percentile among goalies. Goals saved above expected measures exactly that gap: what a goalie stops against what the shots deserved.

The problem is the hardest chances. He is stopping .583 on high-danger shots against a league .685, and he is below average on low- and medium-danger shots too, so this isn't one unlucky band. His last five starts were 6.42 goals below expected. Last season was also below expected by our numbers (6.8 in 50 games), though Evolving-Hockey's model had him on the positive side, and had him excellent the year before that. Eleven games is still a small sample for a goalie, but for a Cup winner (Colorado, 2022) with this much track record, the next few weeks matter for Los Angeles.
